title: KV cache eviction & long-context troubleshooting - Orion Analytics
next_steps: Redwood to share KV-cache eviction diagnostic script and benchmark results link
Orion to run benchmark on staging (sample workload) and share logs by 2025-10-15
Schedule follow-up deep dive with Orion infra team week of 2025-10-20
summary: Deep dive on KV-cache eviction patterns observed by Orion Analytics during long-context sessions. Covered eviction triggers (memory pressure vs fragmentation/pinning bugs), paging to host memory, prefix reuse strategies, batching tradeoffs for latency/throughput, and implications for Dedicated vs Private (VPC) deployments. Agreed next steps: Redwood share diagnostic script and benchmark harness; Orion run staging benchmark and capture KV metrics; follow-up meeting to review logs and tune cache settings.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: ok everyone, thanks for joining, we've got about an hour, the goal is to dig into the KV-cache eviction and paging behavior you hit in production. alex is our SE, he'll drive the technical bits.
[00:07] Sam Patel: yeah thanks, appreciate it. we've been seeing steady cache evictions when sessions go past ~32k tokens, and the tail latency spikes. we've tried increasing kv cache size but eviction still happens.
[00:20] Alex Rivera: cool. quick clarifying q, when you say 32k tokens is that per request or cumulative for the session prefix?
[00:29] Lina Gomez: it's cumulative; we have long-running chat sessions where users append and the prefix is reused across multiple requests. some sessions hit 40k+ tokens.
[00:36] Alex Rivera: ok that helps. two common patterns: one is memory pressure on the GPU leading to eviction, second is our paging/eviction heuristic when the KV entries exceed the configured cache window or when fragmentation causes inefficient packing.
[00:52] Marcus Lee: we run on Dedicated nodes with A100-40G. we thought 40G would be fine, but the model plus activations plus kv cache is more than we anticipated.
[01:01] Maya Chen: can you confirm if you're using quantized model variants in Dedicated or full fp16?
[01:07] Sam Patel: fp16 right now. we tried int8 weights for smaller model but the accuracy delta worried product.
[01:14] Alex Rivera: fp16 will mean larger KV entries than int8 sessions. important: KV cache size is proportional to seq_len * d_model * sizeof(float). so quantization can reduce memory but may affect quality.
[01:25] [01:25] Speaker 1: (inaudible) we saw a weird thing where eviction happened mid-request, like a gap, not just between requests.
[01:32] Alex Rivera: mid-request eviction usually implies the runtime decided to evict some KV pages to free memory for the current token computation — essentially paging to host or dropping least-recently-used prefixes. that's usually because peak working memory crossed the threshold during attention compute.
[01:45] Lina Gomez: is that deterministic? sometimes we see different behavior for identical traffic patterns.
[01:50] Alex Rivera: there are a couple of sources of non-determinism: concurrent workloads on the same GPU, transient fragmentation, and background defragmentation routines. also if multiple sessions share the same allocation pool, allocation order can change.
[02:05] Sam Patel: ok got it. for our use-case we rely on prefix reuse a lot — we intentionally cache large conversation history to avoid re-encoding. any specific settings to recommend?
[02:14] Alex Rivera: yes. two levers: pinned prefixes and max_cached_tokens per session. pinned prefixes mark KV entries as ineligible for eviction except under severe pressure; they cost memory but preserve reuse. max_cached_tokens bounds per-session KV size to avoid one session starving others.
[02:30] Maya Chen: note that pinned prefixes are a paid-dedicated policy in Redwood Dedicated, but they also exist in Private with config flags.
[02:39] Marcus Lee: we hadn't seen the pinned prefix option documented. can you send docs?
[02:42] Alex Rivera: i'll drop the doc link in follow-up — it's a config flag plus a runtime knob. we also have a diagnostic script that prints per-session KV metrics (entries, bytes, last-accessed).
[02:55] Sam Patel: yes please, logs would help. we saw eviction logs like "kv_cache_evicted session_id=... reason=memory_pressure" but not much else.
[03:03] Alex Rivera: ok we'll share the eviction diagnostic and a small benchmark harness you can run on staging. the harness emulates prefix reuse patterns and measures tail latency, eviction count, and paging events.
[03:14] [03:14] Speaker 2: question — how does batching interact with cache reuse? we've seen higher throughput when batching but worse tail latency for specific sessions.
[03:20] Alex Rivera: good question. batching increases throughput by coalescing token steps across sessions, but it increases peak memory during the token step. larger batch sizes mean more simultaneous KV accesses and hold more activations in memory, raising eviction risk. smaller batches reduced peak memory but cost throughput. it's a tradeoff.
[03:36] Lina Gomez: we currently use dynamic batching with max batch 16. is there a recommended sweet spot?
[03:41] Alex Rivera: depends on your latency SLO. for A100-40G, we often see good tradeoffs at batch 4-8 for long-context workloads if you also enable prefix trimming and max_cached_tokens. also continuous batching policies that prioritize low-latency lanes help.
[03:56] Sam Patel: any recommendations around prefix trimming heuristics? we have some system messages and rarely used tokens we could trim.
[04:03] Alex Rivera: yes — apply TTL for older turns (e.g., keep last N tokens fully cached, compress/hypersummary older history into a condensed prefix), and use frequency-based retention for reused prompts. prefix compression (summaries) is often the most cost-effective.
[04:16] Marcus Lee: about paging — you mentioned paging to host memory. does that mean if KV is evicted it gets moved to CPU RAM and then loaded back? What's the perf impact?
[04:25] Alex Rivera: exactly. paging to host creates a O(10-50x) latency penalty on a per-chunk fetch depending on PCIe/InfiniBand and host memory speed; it can be less on NVLink. So if your workload causes repeated page in/out, tail latency will spike. Our runtime tries to avoid thrashing by grouping adjacent pages and prefetching, but if working set larger than GPU memory, prefetches may not help.
[04:45] Lina Gomez: we are on cloud VPC with NVLink across some nodes, but not all. sometimes we fall back to PCIe.
[04:52] Alex Rivera: that's important — Dedicated with NVLink fabric improves paging significantly; Private on-prem with NVSwitch is best. In VPC without NVLink, paging costs are higher. You may want to isolate heavy long-context sessions to nodes with NVLink or increase max_cached_tokens per node.
[05:07] Sam Patel: is there an automated policy to pin hot prefixes to NVLink nodes?
[05:11] Alex Rivera: we have a smart routing policy that can prefer NVLink-enabled pools for sessions flagged as long-context; it requires tagging the workload. We can walk through config.
[05:20] Maya Chen: quick note on security — if you go Private (VPC) with pinned prefixes, we'll need to coordinate KMS/HSM for encryption of persisted pages if you enable host paging and have stricter compliance.
[05:31] Marcus Lee: noted. we will share compliance constraints.
[05:34] [05:34] Speaker 3: filler — sometimes the transcripts say KV cash, that's a mis transcription.
[05:39] Alex Rivera: haha yeah, KV cash not cash.
[05:41] Sam Patel: ok, on diagnostics: what specific metrics should we capture in staging?
[05:45] Alex Rivera: per-session cached_tokens, kv_bytes_allocated, eviction_count, paging_events (page_in, page_out), last_access_ts, allocation_fragments, and GPU free memory over time. We'll provide a script that emits these to stdout and optionally to Prometheus format.
[06:00] Lina Gomez: can you also include model traces for attention memory peaks?
[06:04] Alex Rivera: yes — we can instrument attention peaks per token step. that'll help correlate eviction timing with compute peaks.
[06:11] Sam Patel: on the model side, would moving to a quantized int8 path be worthwhile? we worry about hallucination/quality.
[06:19] Alex Rivera: int8 or mixed precision quantization reduces KV and weight memory; often you can maintain quality with quantization-aware fine-tuning or calibration. We recommend A/B testing on a held-out eval prompt set; Redwood Optimize has a quantization recommendation pipeline if you want us to run it as part of the POC.
[06:36] Marcus Lee: what's the effort to enable pinned-prefixes and routing policies on Dedicated? we have a reseller contract timeline so want to plan.
[06:44] Maya Chen: pinned prefixes are a config change plus a billing flag for guaranteed reservation; routing policies require a short config change and we'll validate with capacity planner. we can include estimated incremental cost in the follow-up pricing doc.
[06:57] Alex Rivera: also note there are kernel-level optimizations: for certain transformer implementations we can compress KV layout to reduce fragmentation; that's model-specific and would be part of the optimization engineering work if you want Redwood R&D to assist.
[07:12] Sam Patel: yes please — we'd like Redwood to help on an optimization pass if benchmarks show benefit.
[07:18] Lina Gomez: for the benchmark harness, can you support both NVLink and PCIe mode emulation?
[07:23] Alex Rivera: we can. harness will run with flags to simulate PCIe-only and NVLink paging latencies; it will also emit synthetic trace showing page_in/out counts.
[07:31] Maya Chen: ok let's recap quickly and call out action owners.
[07:35] Sam Patel: yep.
[07:36] Maya Chen: Redwood: Alex will share the eviction diagnostic script, benchmark harness, and pinned-prefix docs. (action: Alex)
[07:44] Alex Rivera: confirmed. I'll put links in the follow-up email and a small readme on how to run the harness.
[07:50] Maya Chen: Orion: Sam/Lina will run the harness on staging, collect logs, and share by 2025-10-15. (action: Sam/Lina)
[07:58] Sam Patel: confirmed.
[08:00] Maya Chen: we'll schedule a follow-up technical deep dive on the week of 2025-10-20 to review results and review potential pinned-prefix rollout. I'll include cost estimates.
[08:10] Marcus Lee: thanks everyone. one last q — are there any quick config flags we can flip that are low-risk now?
[08:16] Alex Rivera: yes: reduce max dynamic batch size (e.g., from 16 to 8), enable prefix TTL trimming for turns older than X, and enable our eviction_debug logging to capture more context — all safe to toggle on staging.
[08:29] Lina Gomez: we'll try those and include results in the logs.
[08:33] Maya Chen: great. thanks all. follow-up items in email.
[08:36] Sam Patel: thanks.
[08:37] [END]
